snapshot.what_it_does: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), founded in 1968 and part of the Tata Group, is an IT services, consulting and business solutions organisation that partners with many of the world's largest businesses on transformation journeys, offering application development and management, digital transformation, AI, data and cloud services, engineering services, cognitive business operations, cyber security, and products & platforms. With over 580,000 consultants across 56 countries and 194 service delivery centres, it has set an aspiration to become the world's largest AI-led technology services company, positioning itself as a full-stack AI services player from infrastructure to intelligence, and generated consolidated revenues of US$30 billion (₹267,021 crore) in fiscal 2026.

snapshot.geographies: TCS has an extensive footprint spanning North America, Latin America, the United Kingdom, Continental Europe, Asia Pacific, India and Middle East Africa (p55). Standalone FY2026 revenue by customer location: Americas ₹1,21,267 crore (including US ₹1,16,393 crore), Europe ₹64,648 crore (including UK ₹40,613 crore), India ₹15,101 crore, Others ₹19,922 crore (p293).
key_facts: Consolidated FY2026 revenue of ₹267,021 crore (US$30 billion), growth of 4.6% over the previous year (p9, p36)
Operating margin of 25.0% and net margin of 19.8%, both the highest in the last four years; net income ₹52,820 crore, up 8.8% (p9)
Total contract value of US$40.7 billion, with 5 mega deals signed during the year (p6, p9)
Annualised revenues of US$2.3 billion in AI services and US$11.5 billion in new-age services (Cloud, Data, Enterprise Solutions, Cyber Security) (p9)
Total dividend of ₹110 per share for FY2026, including a recommended final dividend of ₹31 per share (p9)

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Mixed credibility: segment and cash-return promises (BFSI, manufacturing, dividends, wage-hike impact) were kept, but the repeated march toward the 26-28% margin band went backwards to 24% and FY26 constant-currency growth declined. Directional optimism on growth proved accurate; margin aspirations did not.

bull.point: Revenue momentum improved: Q4 FY26 ₹70,698cr (+9.6% YoY), Q1 FY27 +13.9%, Q2 +11.2%; FY26 TCV US$40.7bn with 5 mega deals.
Profitability and cash returns remain strong: FY26 operating margin 25.0%, net margin 19.8%, net income ₹52,820cr (+8.8%), dividend ₹110/share.
AI optionality is real: US$2.3bn annualised AI services and US$11.5bn new-age services, backed by 580,000 consultants across 56 countries.

bear.point: Underlying demand weaker than reported: FY26 constant-currency revenue fell 2.4% YoY while reported grew 4.6%; developed-market growth promise was missed.
bear.cite: promised_vs_delivered Q4 FY26 p7; snapshot p9

bear.point: Margin credibility strained: op margin slid from 25.3% Q4 FY26 to 24.0% in Q1/Q2 FY27; wage hikes cut 170bps, 26-28% band unmet.
Earnings quality uneven: Q3 FY26 PAT fell 13.9% YoY despite +4.9% revenue; Q2 FY27 PAT rose 15% but margin stayed 24%.

watch: Q3 FY27 operating margin: whether H2 inch-up and FY27 25%+ EBIT exit promise starts delivering.
Constant-currency international growth, especially BFSI and manufacturing sustaining Q2 FY27 momentum.
TCV/mega-deal conversion into revenue and evidence AI annualised revenue is scaling beyond US$2.3bn.
